extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (agents/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards from the MPEP change summary for examiners and practitioners on prior art, obviousness, claim construction, enablement, and related procedural exceptions under AIA and pre‑AIA law. Covers how examiners should establish rejections, what evidence may be considered, and applicant rebuttal/exception procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of AIA vs pre‑AIA law
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies when AIA and pre‑AIA law apply to examination and that many sections are applicable regardless of whether an application is examined under the AIA or under pre‑AIA law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor Notes add cross references and repeatedly clarify applicability; sections were revised to remove citations inappropriate to applicability (e.g., removing Phillips v. AWH). See cross references throughout MPEP (e.g., §§ 2117, 2143, 2154.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consulting extrinsic evidence in claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance to include discussion and citation to Phillips v. AWH Corp. (415 F.3d 1303) regarding consulting extrinsic evidence in claim construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated citations and discussions emphasize proper role of extrinsic evidence in claim meaning determinations; see added discussion in relevant subsections and cross references (e.g., Corephotonics/Apple citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim term meaning provided by the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where previously the phrase 'special definition' was used, the manual replaces it with 'meaning provided by the specification.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should look to the specification for the meaning of claim terms and treat any specification‑provided meaning as authoritative for claim construction unless other governing law requires otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.130 affidavit/declaration exceptions (attribution/prior public disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies that an exception in a 37 CFR 1.130 affidavit or declaration may be of attribution or prior public disclosure and explains how prior art could be antedated under pre‑AIA law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moved pre‑AIA guidance to a new item to clarify differences; guidance explains when 1.130 is available and when its provisions do not apply; see cross references to MPEP § 717.01(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic publications and Wayback Machine as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Replaces 'Prior art disclosures' with 'Electronic publications' and clarifies guidance regarding use of the Wayback Machine®.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides updated procedures and cautionary notes for treating web/archived content as printed publications; includes cross references and editorial clarifications about evaluating such evidence's reliability and dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.14(a) and copending applications (shared inventorship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies that 37 CFR 1.14(a) applies to all pending U.S. 'patent' applications and that rejections may be made when copending applications have 'at least one' inventor in common or differ by at least one 'joint' inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may make rejections based on copendency when inventor overlap exists; text streamlined for clarity on inventor/inventorship terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogous art requirement for combining references
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than one prior art reference is used as the basis of an obviousness rejection, it is not required that the references be analogous art to each other but they must be analogous art to the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added citations and examples (e.g., Sanofi‑Aventis v. Mylan; Corephotonics v. Apple) clarifying that analogy is measured to the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation to combine: result‑effective variable not sole motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of a result‑effective variable is one, but not the only, motivation for a person of ordinary skill in the art to experiment to reach another workable product or process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross references to MPEP § 2144.05, subsection II.B; examiners should consider multiple rationales for motivation to combine and not rely solely on presence of a result‑effective variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: If modification renders prior art unsatisfactory, there may be no motivation to combine
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposed modification would render the prior art invention being modified unsatisfactory for its intended purpose, there 'may be' no suggestion or motivation to make the proposed modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should evaluate whether modification would defeat the purpose of the asserted prior art; lack of motivation can defeat an obviousness rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non‑prior‑art references to establish level of ordinary skill
rubrics_metrics.description: References which are not prior art may be relied upon to demonstrate the level of ordinary skill in the art at or around the relevant time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such references may be cited to show the level of skill or motivation even if they are not prior art; MPEP text was clarified to explain how to use these references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant rebuttal rights to prima facie obviousness conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may submit rebuttal arguments, in addition to or as an alternative to evidence, in response to a prima facie conclusion of obviousness produced by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies where rebuttal arguments can be presented, types of admissible declarations under AIA and pre‑AIA, and cross references to MPEP §§ 714–716, 715.09, and specific examples added or revised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official notice: use should be rare and cautious
rubrics_metrics.description: Reorganized discussion of official notice and guidance that it should be rarely used; not advisable to rely on official notice when an examiner can find a prior art disclosure to support the fact at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official notice should be used sparingly, especially when application is under final rejection or action under 37 CFR 1.113; see reorganization and reminder statements in subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graham factual findings required to establish prima facie obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Office personnel must consider the factors in Graham v. John Deere to establish a prima facie case of obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added cross references to MPEP §§ 714.12, 714.13, and others; examiners must identify and make Graham factual findings (scope/content of prior art, differences, level of ordinary skill, and secondary considerations) when making obviousness rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each reference used as basis for obviousness must be prior art and analogous to the claimed invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reference 'to be applied as the basis for an obviousness rejection' must qualify as prior art and must also be analogous art 'to the claimed invention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit clarity added to subsection II.A.1; ensure each cited reference meets both prior art status and analogy requirements before combining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact‑findings must state a rationale supporting obviousness (KSR requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact‑findings should state a rationale, as required by KSR, that supports a conclusion that the claimed invention would have been obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated subsection II.A.5 and added supporting citations (KSR Int'l Co. v. Teleflex) — examiners must articulate a reasoned rationale for the combination beyond naked conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable expectation of success defined for obviousness analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The reasonable expectation of success requirement refers to the likelihood of success in combining or modifying prior art disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble and subsection text clarify that the focus is likelihood of success in achieving the claimed solution by combining or modifying prior art; added citations (Elekta v. ZAP, Intelligent Bio‑Sys, Eli Lilly v. Teva).

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching, suggestion, or motivation in the prior art is an appropriate rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: A teaching, suggestion, or motivation to combine references that is found in the prior art is an appropriate rationale for determining obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection X.C added this clarification with citations to KSR; examiners may rely on explicit teachings/suggestions in the prior art as part of their rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary considerations (objective indicia) must be considered when properly presented
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence pertaining to secondary considerations must be taken into account whenever 'it has been properly presented.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions clarify how and when secondary considerations (commercial success, long felt need, etc.) should be considered and include cross references to MPEP §§ 715 et seq., 716 et seq., and examples revised/added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim nonobviousness can be impacted by effective filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim depending from a nonobvious independent claim may not be nonobvious when the effective filing date of a dependent claim is later than the effective filing date of an independent claim from which the dependent claim depends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that priority/effective date differences can change the obviousness analysis for dependent claims; see preamble updates and cross references to §§ 2133.01 and 2152.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's reply may establish that a disclosure is not prior art or is disqualified
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant's reply may establish that a disclosure is not prior art or is disqualified as prior art (e.g., by showing common ownership, inventor‑originated disclosure, or other exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added guidance that applicant replies can rebut prior art status and cross references to MPEP §§ 2146, 2153.01, 2154.02, 2155; examiners should consider such replies where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period and inventor‑originated disclosure exceptions under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A)/(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that the exception under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A) may apply if the disclosure was the inventor's (or at least one joint inventor's) own work; 102(b)(1)(B) may apply if the reference discloses subject matter that was 'previously' publicly disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to show an inventor‑originated disclosure is not prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1); format specified in 37 CFR 1.77(b)(6) may not be used after the filing date; applicants may include statements regarding such disclosures in the specification upon or after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint research agreement (JRA) exception procedure and corroboration standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified guidance on invoking the JRA exception (AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C)), including statement formatting and fee requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement should be on or begin on a separate page (cross reference to MPEP § 717.02(a)(1), subsection II); guidance on when processing fee required to amend specification; Office will not request corroborating evidence unless doubt exists as to existence or nature of the JRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) prior art and limits under 102(b)(2)(A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified discussion regarding when a reference qualifies as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) and that 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(A) limits use of an inventor's or at least one joint inventor's own work as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaced phrasing to emphasize 'disclosures in potential prior art references' and added cross references and examples; clarifies commonly owned/deemed commonly owned disclosures treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic Drinkware applicability limited to pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Added explanation that Dynamic Drinkware only applies to applications and patents subject to pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and does not apply to AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added a cross reference to MPEP § 2154.01(b) and clarified distinctions between pre‑AIA and AIA provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement: quantity of experimentation (post‑Amgen/Sanofi guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated to incorporate 'Guidelines for Assessing Enablement' in view of the Supreme Court decision in Amgen Inc. v. Sanofi; subsection title updated to 'Quantity of Experimentation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added citations and quotations from Amgen v. Sanofi and related Federal Circuit decisions; examiners should apply the updated enablement guidelines when assessing whether the specification enables the full scope of the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective standard for measuring scope of subjective claim terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should determine whether the specification supplies some objective standard for measuring the scope of a subjective term used in the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection IV clarified this duty; where subjective terms are used, examiners should look for objective measures in the specification to fix claim scope (and cite In re Kiely and Clearone v. Shure decisions as guidance).
